title: CBS Covers Florida Charter Schools
author: Peter Greene
summary: Mainstream media finally documented charter school operators' self-dealing practices in Florida, highlighting how they establish shell companies and management contracts to extract taxpayer education dollars for private profit. The CBS segment featured education funding expert Bruce Baker discussing mechanisms through which charter operators hire their own companies to drain public resources while Erika Donalds emerged as a key figure promoting school choice policies that benefit operators over students. The reporting exemplifies how mainstream journalism validated years of advocate warnings about the perverse incentives created when charter operators can funnel public education funds to private interests. This investigation demonstrates that public awareness of charter financial schemes remains dangerously limited despite a decade of critical voices questioning charter accountability gaps. Greene uses ironic tone throughout, suggesting the obviousness of such practices while praising mainstream media for finally noticing what advocates have documented for over a decade.
points: Mainstream media investigation confirmed charter operators create self-dealing arrangements where they hire their own companies to extract taxpayer education dollars for private interests.
Charter school grifting in Florida involves operators establishing shell companies and lucrative management contracts that funnel public dollars to private gain without public scrutiny.
The practice concentrates wealth among charter owners while public school students lose educational resources and funding stability.
Erika Donalds emerged as a prominent figure in Florida's school choice agenda, promoting policies that prioritize charter operator interests over student outcomes.
Public awareness of charter financial schemes remains surprisingly limited despite years of advocate documentation and warnings about accountability gaps.
